# Ensure every Main Street card has a dedicated 64×64 sprite

## Goal

As a player, every Main Street card shows distinct, recognisable art in its 64×64 left-art zone — no card falls back to the generic `Fallback` sprite in the market, hand, or street.

## Context

discovered-from:CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN

The 64×64 left-art redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN, commit 38cf1f08) embeds a 64×64 sprite PNG into every card face and resolves it by card name via `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` (generated by `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`), falling back to the `Fallback` sprite when no dedicated sprite exists.

Today only 63 sprites exist for the 171 card templates in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, so ~108 cards render the same generic `Fallback` art. The gaps:

- **Upgrade cards (39)** — names like `Upgrade to Patisserie`; many have a `targetBusiness` that does resolve to a sprite (e.g. `Diner`, `Hardware Store`, `Boutique`), so at minimum upgrades can inherit their target's art.
- **Staff cards (25)** — no sprites (`Assistant`, `Chef`, `Security Guard`, …).
- **Event cards (~44)** — no sprites (`Rainy Day`, `Block Party`, `Tax Audit`, …).

## Proposed approach

Decide the art strategy per family (to confirm during intake/plan):

1. **Upgrades** — derive art from `targetBusiness` (or an explicit override when `targetBusiness` is empty), so each upgrade shows the business it enhances.
2. **Staff** — add role/family sprites or a small set of shared staff art.
3. **Events** — add per-event sprites or a documented category mapping (e.g. incident vs opportunity, festival vs economic).

Then extend the resolver and/or art map accordingly, keeping `Fallback` only as a genuine last resort.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card in `card-data.csv` resolves via `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite (any documented mapping/alias counts).
2. Upgrade cards resolve to a sprite derived from their `targetBusiness` (or a documented explicit override); no upgrade shows generic `Fallback` art.
3. Staff cards each resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card shows generic `Fallback` art.
4. Event cards each resolve to dedicated or category-mapped art; no event card shows generic `Fallback` art.
5. A regression test asserts AC 1–4 (a drift guard over `card-data.csv`), and `Fallback` remains in the map/resolver for genuinely-unknown/future cards.
6. Docs (`docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`, `public/assets/CREDITS.md`) document the mapping rules and any new art's licence/attribution.
7. `npm run build` is green and the unit test suite passes.

## Risks / notes

- **Art strategy is a design decision** — unique art for 108 cards is a large asset effort; reuse/mapping (especially upgrades → target business) may be the pragmatic first step. Confirm scope with the producer.
- Any new art must be permissively licensed (CC0/MIT/Apache) and attributed in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Mapping changes must be mirrored in both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`).

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types.

## Problem

`rasteriseSvgToTexture()` in `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` hard-codes a 4x oversampling factor:

```ts
const qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr);
const targetW = Math.round(width * qualityScale);
```

Every card SVG is therefore rasterised at 4x its logical size (a 140x80 card becomes a 560x320 canvas) regardless of how large it is actually drawn. Consequences:

- The 64x64 art zone within that SVG occupies 256x256 device pixels, forcing the embedded bitmap to be upscaled 4x (see CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R for the complementary embedded-art fix).
- ~16x more texture memory and GPU upload bandwidth than the display actually needs.
- Texture cache keys encode the logical size + DPR, not the rendered size, so every card is over-allocated.

## Proposed change

Rasterise at the display native resolution: `qualityScale = dpr` (i.e. render at `width x dpr`), so textures are allocated at exactly the device pixels they occupy. Retain a small supersample (e.g. 1x) for the vector stroke/text quality if visual review shows artefacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `rasteriseSvgToTexture()` no longer hard-codes a 4x multiplier; the render resolution is derived from the display density (DPR)
2. Existing `SvgHelpers` unit/browser tests are updated to assert the new resolution contract
3. Card textures are allocated at `width * dpr` (verified by a test asserting canvas dimensions)
4. No visual regression in card text/vector stroke legibility (reviewed at DPR 1, 2 and 3)
5. Unit tests pass (`npm test -- --project unit`)
6. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)

## Interaction with CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R

The two fixes are complementary. Reducing the SVG rasterisation to native resolution lowers the required embedded-art resolution; raising the embedded art makes the card crisp at any rasterisation scale. Decide the final art resolution (64x64, 128x128 or 256x256) once this change lands.

## Open question (producer review)

Interpretation of "native resolution" in the request is ambiguous. This work item assumes it means "the display native resolution (DPR-matched)" rather than the 4x quality scale. If instead it means "generate the card SVG canvas at a higher intrinsic size (e.g. 560x320 native with a 256x256 art zone)", the ACs above should be rewritten. Confirm before implementing.
data.title: Render card SVGs at native resolution instead of 4x quality upsampling

## Problem

`implement.py finish` removes the worktree and pushes the feature branch into `dev` **from the main checkout** (`repo_root`). The pre-push context-budget gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) measures the **working tree of the push source** — so when the commit being pushed changes `AGENTS.md`/thresholds, the main checkout is still at the old (breaching) dev state and the gate rejects the push, even though the pushed commit is compliant.

Observed while implementing CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ: `finish` passed build + full suite, committed `85ae7038`, then failed the push with `Context budget exceeded committed thresholds`. The commit had to be pushed manually from a worktree at the commit (`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev`), where the gate measured the new files and passed without `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`.

## Impact

Any commit that legitimately changes the startup context surface (e.g. an `AGENTS.md` edit) cannot be pushed by `implement.py finish` without a bypass, undermining the gate and forcing manual recovery.

## Options

1. `finish` pushes from the worktree (new files present) before removing it, rather than from the main checkout.
2. The hook measures the **pushed commit** (e.g. `git show <local-sha>:AGENTS.md`) instead of the working tree.
3. `finish` fast-forwards the local parent branch to the commit before pushing.

Discovered during CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ; recovered manually.

# Chore: Document config-driven game catalogue + create per-game build presets

## Problem statement

The config-driven game catalogue (`configs/*.json` presets + `GAMES_CONFIG`)
is only described briefly and in two places (README and the Developer Guide),
with no single authoritative reference covering the preset schema, resolution
order, the `GAME_INFO` convention, or how to author a new preset. The shipped
presets are distribution-oriented (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full`);
none selects a *specific named game*, so a developer cannot build or run, for
example, Main Street in isolation from the launcher checkout.

## Users and user stories

- As a **game developer**, I want to build/run one specific game in isolation so
  I can iterate quickly without pulling in the other games, using
  `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>`.
- As an **engine maintainer**, I want one authoritative document describing how
  build presets are structured, resolved and created, so I can add a preset
  correctly without reverse-engineering the plugin.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the README to keep a concise summary and
  link to the detailed doc, so the high-traffic entry point stays short while
  the full contract is discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README keeps a concise "Which games does a build include?" section and links
   to a dedicated detailed document (`docs/dev/game-configuration.md`) for full
   details, replacing the current `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`
   anchor as the primary reference.
2. The detailed document describes the preset schema in full: the top-level
   `games` array; required `id`, `path`, `scenePath`; optional `adapterPath`,
   `siblingScenePath` and `siblingAdapterPath` (the `src/`-layout sibling
   fields, Option C); the non-schema `$comment` annotation; preset selection
   (`GAMES_CONFIG` preset name or explicit path, default `core-only`); the
   three-step resolution order (`<root>/<scenePath>` →
   `<path>/<siblingScenePath>` → `<path>/<scenePath>`); the always-present
   core-owned Gym; the `GAME_INFO` convention and parsing; and
   validation/failure modes. It explains what each shipped preset (distribution
   and per-game) is and how it is structured — not only one example.
3. A per-game preset exists at `configs/<game-id>.json` for every example game —
   `beleaguered-castle`, `blackjack`, `coloretto`, `feudalism`, `golf`,
   `lost-cities`, `main-street`, `sushi-go` — each containing exactly that one
   game entry (Gym is always added by the plugin).
4. `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>` selects exactly that game (+ Gym): the generated
   registry for each per-game preset imports the game's scene class and no other
   game, and one representative per-game preset is verified with a real
   `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id> npm run build`.
5. Unit tests guard every per-game preset: each ships exactly one game, uses the
   sibling `../tce-<id>` path form, resolves to a real scene module with the
   expected scene class, and generates a catalogue containing that game + Gym and
   no other game. Existing distribution-preset and discovery-plugin tests still
   pass.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: the README
   summary section, the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` catalogue section, the new
   `docs/dev/game-configuration.md`, `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`
   where it references `configs/*.json` presets, and the preset/`GAME_INFO`
   doc comment in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (which still lists
   the pre-rename preset names `core-only`, `all` and `sample`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break the existing distribution presets (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/
  `deluxe`/`full`) or their tests; per-game presets are additive.
- Presets are data only — no plugin/behaviour change is required (the plugin
  already iterates `games`).
- UK English in all prose.

## Existing state

- Build presets: `configs/{core-only,solo,arcade,deluxe,full}.json`
  (renamed from `core-only/sample/all` in commit `1b6c84b6`).
- Discovery plugin: `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (`selectConfigPath`,
  `loadGamesConfig`, `discoverGames`, `renderGameRegistryModule`,
  `selectedGameIds`).
- Tests: `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` (a `PRESET_GAMES` map),
  `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`.
- Docs: `README.md` ("Which games does a build include?"), `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  ("Config-Driven Game Catalogue"), `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- Known doc drift: the plugin's header doc comment
  (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) still names the pre-rename presets
  `core-only`, `all` and `sample`; correct it to the shipped
  `core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full` set.
- Deployment note: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` currently builds the default
  (`core-only`) preset — covered by the separate work item CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Desired change

Add eight per-game presets (`configs/<game-id>.json`), add a dedicated
`docs/dev/game-configuration.md` reference, trim/link the README section to it,
and extend the preset tests to cover the per-game set.

## Key Files

- `configs/<game-id>.json` — eight new per-game presets (one game entry each).
- `docs/dev/game-configuration.md` — new authoritative reference for the preset
  schema, resolution, `GAME_INFO` convention and authoring steps.
- `README.md` — concise summary + link to the new doc.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — point the catalogue section at the new doc; keep the
  workflow summary.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — cross-reference the per-game presets
  alongside the existing `configs/*.json` mention.
- `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` — extend `PRESET_GAMES` (or add a
  per-game guard) for the eight per-game presets.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — doc comment cross-reference only
  (no behaviour change expected).

## Related work

- CG-0MTRO6Y2N009B9CF — Config-driven game discovery (Vite plugin + configs/).
- CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC — Launcher distribution with configs/ presets (solo/
  arcade/deluxe/full).
- CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X — Documentation for the multi-repo workflow.
- CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1 — Deploy full engine with all games via `GAMES_CONFIG=all`
  (deployment follow-on).
- CG-0MLVJR7JI0YF87IN — Game Selector: Fix card layout for 4+ games (completed;
  the selector must render the growing per-preset catalogue cleanly).
- CG-0MSKVOSW3004HZVB — Verify full suite green with documented deps (completed;
  establishes the test baseline this change must keep green).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** per-game presets are named `configs/<game-id>.json` (so
  `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street`), matching the `id` used everywhere else.
- **Assumption:** the existing distribution presets are kept as-is; per-game
  presets are additive (`solo.json` remains a golf distribution preset even
  though `configs/golf.json` also selects golf).
- **Risk (low):** preset proliferation / maintenance (13 presets). Mitigated by
  a test that derives the per-game set from the game list rather than hand-listing.
- **Risk (low):** doc drift between README, DEVELOPER.md and the new doc.
  Mitigated by making the new doc the single detailed reference and linking from
  both.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the `deploy.yml` `GAMES_CONFIG` change is out of scope
  here and tracked by CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview questions were required. Requirements were stated explicitly by
  the operator: (a) keep the README configuration section brief and link to a
  separate document; (b) the separate document must explain how configurations
  are created and structured — not just describe one example preset; (c) create
  one configuration per game so each game can be built in isolation.
- The preset renaming to `solo/arcade/deluxe/full` (commit `1b6c84b6`) landed
  during this session; this brief reflects the post-rename state.

The GitHub Pages deployment only publishes the Gym (core engine demo), not the full set of example games listed in `configs/full.json`.

## Solution

Update the "Build" step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to select the all-games preset:

```yaml
- name: Build
  run: GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build
```

The config-driven game discovery plugin (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) reads `configs/full.json`, which lists all 8 games. Each game is resolved locally first (`example-games/<id>/...`) then as a sibling repo (`../tce-<id>/...`), so this works whether building from the launcher checkout or from a single-game repo.

> **Preset name corrected (plan, 2026-09-26):** this item originally referenced `GAMES_CONFIG=all` / `configs/all.json`. No such preset exists anywhere in the repository. `selectConfigPath()` treats an unknown preset name as a **hard error** (deliberately: it never silently falls back, because that would ship a distribution missing the requested games), so a literal implementation of the original wording would break the Pages build. The canonical "every game" preset is **`full`** (`configs/full.json`) — evidenced by `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`, `configs/full.json`'s own `$comment`, CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC AC5 (`full=all`), and `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` which pins the named-preset contract. ## Outline

Card hover highlight in Lost Cities does not match the actual card size — it is too short vertically (top and bottom) because the tint overlay uses a hardcoded `CARD_H` (130px) instead of the game's `HAND_CARD_H` (137px).

## Problem

Lost Cities uses 100x137 card dimensions (`HAND_CARD_W`/`HAND_CARD_H`), but the shared `HandView` tint overlay system in `src/ui/HandView._setCardTint()` hardcodes `CARD_H` (130) as the overlay height. This means the hover highlight (green tint overlay) is 7px shorter than the actual card.

Additionally, Lost Cities does not pass `cardHeight` in its HandView construction options, so `this.cardHeight` also defaults to `CARD_H` (130).

## Root cause

| Location | What | Expected | Actual |
|----------|------|----------|--------|
| `src/ui/HandView.ts:1896` | Overlay height in `_setCardTint()` | `this.cardHeight` | `CARD_H` (130) |
| `LostCitiesRenderer.ts` HandView options | `cardHeight` option | `HAND_CARD_H` (137) | not passed (defaults to 130) |

Note: `this.cardWidth` is correctly set to `HAND_CARD_W` (100) via the HandView options, which is why the hover highlight width appears correct.

## Fix

1. **`src/ui/HandView.ts` line ~1896**: Change the overlay height from `CARD_H` to `this.cardHeight`
2. **`example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts`**: Add `cardHeight: HAND_CARD_H` to the HandView construction options

## Acceptance Criteria

- Card hover highlight (green tint overlay) matches the card display size exactly — no visible gap at top/bottom
- All Lost Cities card types (numbered, investment, action) show consistent hover highlights
- Other games using HandView (Gym, Main Street, Golf, Sushi Go, Beleaguered Castle, Blackjack) are unaffected — hover highlights continue to work correctly
- Full project test suite passes

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `_setCardTint()` overlay creation (~line 1896)
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — `CARD_H` (130) default
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts` — HandView construction (~line 546)

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,
   `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`,
   `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`.
2. Each repository's default branch contains the extracted,
   history-preserving tree in the F9 `src/` layout (extraction via
   `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, scaffold via `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`):
   the core repo holds the engine + Gym + launcher shell and **no games**; each
   game repo has its source at repo-root `src/` and wires the engine as a
   `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
3. From a **fresh remote clone**, `git clone --recurse-submodules <game-repo>`
   followed by `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm test -- --project unit`

4. The launcher can compose a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings (spot

   from.

Extract all nine repos from the monorepo at the current `dev` HEAD, scaffold the
